summary: QUICK GPU compile/launch test: instantiate the GDN tree-verify scan kernel _tree_gdn_kernel at native geometry (BV=32, num_warps=4) for N_PAD in {2 (cat2), 4, 16 (cat9)} plus the current baseline (BV=16/warps=8/N_PAD=16), and read Triton ptxas n_regs + n_spills + launch success/fail. Empirically confirms WHERE BV=32/warps=4 spills (math predicts: fits at N_PAD<=4, spills at N_PAD=16 ~512 regs >> 255 cap). NO model load - just the Triton kernel compile + a dummy launch. Fast.

test.howMeasured: Wrote a minimal harness /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/output/fr13_spill_test/spill_probe.py that IMPORTS the committed _tree_gdn_kernel from src/lumo_flywheel_serving/fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py UNCHANGED and launches it DIRECTLY via _tree_gdn_kernel[grid](...) so BLOCK_V and num_warps can be overridden (the launcher hardcodes BV=16 / num_warps=8). For each config it builds dummy CUDA tensors of the exact validated shapes the launcher expects (q/k=(n,16,128) bf16, v=(n,48,128) bf16, raw_a/raw_b=(n,48) bf16, A_log/dt_bias=(48,) fp32, h0 bank=(20,48,128,128) fp32, int32 strict/visible masks n_pad x n_pad, out, state), grid=(NUM_VH, cdiv(DIM_V,BV)), constexprs N_ACTUAL=n_pad, N_PAD, DIM_K=128, DIM_V=128, BLOCK_V=BV, RAW_GATING=True, H0_IS_BANK=True, STORE_NODE_STATES=True, and num_warps=W. n_regs and n_spills were read DIRECTLY off the returned Triton compiled-kernel handle as compiled.n_regs / compiled.n_spills (Triton 3.6.0 exposes these as attributes; no ptxas-verbose parsing needed). torch.cuda.synchronize() was called after each launch to force completion and surface CUDA error 701 (too many resources) — none occurred. Ran inside the cu130-nightly vLLM image (vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly) NO-MODEL via: docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --entrypoint python3 -v repo:/repo <image> /repo/output/fr13_spill_test/spill_probe.py. Pre-boot: recover_host_memory() from lumo_flywheel_serving.model_server (OK), free -g showed ~107 GiB free / swap 0, docker ps empty. Results saved to /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/output/fr13_spill_test/results.json.
test.cat2Fits: CONFIRMED. Small trees fit cleanly with zero spill at native geometry (BV=32, num_warps=4). C1 (cat2, N_PAD=2) used 140 regs/thread, 0 spills; C2 (3-4 node tree, N_PAD=4) used 235 regs/thread, 0 spills. Both well under the 255-reg cap. So the cat2 small-tree case matching native's full BV=32/warps=4 geometry compiles and launches with no register spill. (Predicted 64 and 128 regs; measured higher at 140/235 because the kernel carries scan working state, masks, and GDN node-step temporaries on top of the h_cache fp32 tile, but still no spill.)
test.cat9Spills: CONFIRMED that cat9 (N_PAD=16) at native BV=32/warps=4 SPILLS — but the failure mode is a register SPILL, not a hard launch failure. C3 (BV=32, warps=4, N_PAD=16) did NOT raise CUDA 701; ptxas clamped per-thread registers at the 255 architectural cap and spilled the overflow to local memory: n_regs=255, n_spills=636 bytes/thread. The math prediction (512 regs/thread, >> 255 cap) is the right direction — the demand far exceeds 255 so ptxas spills heavily rather than failing the launch. So the prediction's REGISTER-PRESSURE claim is correct; the LAUNCH-FAIL claim is refined: it spills (636 B/thread, severe perf penalty) instead of erroring out. num_warps=4 is the dominant spill driver, as predicted.
test.warps8VsWarps4AtBV32: At BV=32, N_PAD=16 (cat9): going from warps=4 (C3) to warps=8 (C4) cuts spill ~6.6x but does NOT eliminate it. C3 (warps=4): n_regs=255, 636 bytes/thread spilled. C4 (warps=8): n_regs=255, 96 bytes/thread spilled. Doubling warps halves the per-thread share of the h_cache tile (predicted 512 -> 256 regs/thread), which drops the spill from 636 to 96 B/thread, but 256 predicted still exceeds the 255 cap so a residual 96 B/thread spill remains. So extra warps strongly MITIGATE but do not fully AVOID the spill at BV=32/N_PAD=16. Only the current baseline geometry C0 (BV=16, warps=8, N_PAD=16) reaches 0 spill at cat9 size — it sits right at the cap (254 regs) with the BV=16 tile being half the size of BV=32.
test.summary: Measured on GB10 (triton 3.6.0, cu130-nightly, no model): matching native's full geometry (BV=32, num_warps=4) spills our GDN tree-verify scan kernel ONLY at large trees, and the spill scales with N_PAD as predicted. Small trees (cat2, N_PAD=2/4) fit cleanly (0 spill, 140/235 regs). The cat9 tree (N_PAD=16) at BV=32/warps=4 demands ~512 regs/thread vs the 255 cap, so ptxas clamps to 255 and spills 636 bytes/thread — it does NOT throw CUDA 701, it just spills hard (big perf hit). Bumping to warps=8 at BV=32/N_PAD=16 cuts the spill to 96 B/thread (6.6x less) but doesn't clear it; the predicted 256 regs/thread still beats the 255 cap. The current baseline (BV=16, warps=8, N_PAD=16) is the only cat9-size config with zero spill, sitting right at the cap (254 regs). num_warps is confirmed as the dominant spill lever, and BV (16 vs 32, i.e. tile size) is the other. Math prediction confirmed in direction; the only refinement is failure-mode: heavy local-memory spill rather than a launch-time resource error. Artifacts: /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/output/fr13_spill_test/spill_probe.py and /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/output/fr13_spill_test/results.json. No committed kernel source changed; docker left empty, host memory healthy.

verify.numbersReal: REAL — not echoed math. The harness has two fully separate code paths: predicted_regs() (spill_probe.py:49, stored ONLY in the field 'predicted_per_thread_regs') and extract_regs_spills() (lines 92-110), which reads n_regs/n_spills off the returned Triton CompiledKernel handle via getattr(compiled,'n_regs')/getattr(compiled,'n_spills'). These are documented Triton 3.6 CompiledKernel attributes that Triton parses from the ptxas-emitted cubin metadata. The results.json 'method' field is 'compiled.n_regs/.n_spills' for all 5 configs. DECISIVE anti-echo proof: measured n_regs DIVERGES from the prediction in EVERY config — C0 pred128→meas254, C1 pred64→meas140, C2 pred128→meas235, C3 pred512→meas255(clamped), C4 pred256→meas255. If the harness were echoing the math, n_regs would equal predicted_per_thread_regs; it never does. results.json written by root (inside the docker container) at 01:43, device NVIDIA GB10, torch 2.11.0+cu130, triton 3.6.0 — consistent with the cu130-nightly no-model run.
verify.fitsVsSpillsConfirmed: CONFIRMED with correct attribution. A 'fits' claim is only granted when n_spills==0 AND launched==True AND error==None. No config was silently skipped: all 5 report compiled=True, launched=True, error=None (and 'launched' is only set True AFTER torch.cuda.synchronize() succeeds at line 172-173, so a CUDA 701 would be caught into 'error', not mislabeled as launched). FITS: C0 (N_PAD=16,BV=16,w8) 0 spills, C1 (N_PAD=2) 0 spills, C2 (N_PAD=4) 0 spills. SPILLS: C3 (N_PAD=16,BV=32,w4) 636 B/thread, C4 (N_PAD=16,BV=32,w8) 96 B/thread. No config claimed 'fits' while spilling.
verify.matchesMathOrWhy: Matches in DIRECTION; magnitude diverges (correctly flagged in the report). Along the warps=4 BV=32 path: N_PAD=2 fits (140 regs), N_PAD=4 fits (235 regs), N_PAD=16 spills (clamped 255 regs + 636 B spill) — exactly the predicted 'fits ≤N_PAD4, spills at N_PAD16' ordering. Magnitudes are HIGHER than the naive N_PAD*BV*128/(W*32) h_cache-only formula (C1 64→140, C2 128→235) because the kernel carries additional live state beyond the h_cache fp32 tile: per-node scan working state, the strict/visible mask loads, b_q/b_k/b_v GDN node-step temporaries, and l2norm/gating scratch. So the formula under-counts absolute pressure but the SCALING with N_PAD (and the cross-over to spilling) is right. At C3 demand far exceeds the 255 cap so ptxas clamps to 255 and spills — i.e. Triton's layout is 'worse' (more live state) than the formula, not smarter. Refinement to the original prediction: the failure mode is a heavy local-memory SPILL (636 B/thread), NOT a CUDA-701 launch failure — no config raised 701.
verify.warpsIsDominant: CONFIRMED dominant but not sufficient alone. At BV=32, N_PAD=16: C3 (warps=4) spills 636 B/thread; C4 (warps=8) spills 96 B/thread — doubling warps cuts spill 6.6x. However C4 does NOT fully fit (96 B residual spill, n_regs still clamped at 255), so extra warps strongly MITIGATE but do not ELIMINATE the spill at BV=32/N_PAD=16. The only 0-spill cat9-size config is C0 (BV=16, warps=8, N_PAD=16) at 254 regs — which needs BOTH warps=8 AND the smaller BV=16 tile (half the BV=32 tile). So num_warps is the dominant lever and tile size (BV) is the secondary lever; both are needed to clear the cap at N_PAD=16.
verify.cat9NativeGeomReachable: NO — matching native's full geometry (BV=32, num_warps=4) at cat9 (N_PAD=16) is NOT cleanly reachable as-is. C3 does not hard-fail (no CUDA 701) but ptxas clamps registers to the 255 architectural cap and spills 636 bytes/thread to local memory — a severe performance penalty, so it would 'launch' but run badly. Bumping to warps=8 (C4) reduces the spill to 96 B/thread but still does not clear it. The only cat9-size config with zero spill is the CURRENT baseline geometry C0 (BV=16, num_warps=8), at 254 regs right against the cap. Conclusion: cat9 cannot adopt native's exact BV=32/warps=4 geometry without register spilling.
verify.issues: No correctness or integrity issues found. Minor caveats, none of which undermine the verdict: (1) The dummy launch uses random tensors and a synthetic lower-triangular mask, so it validates COMPILE+LAUNCH register/spill behavior only, not numerical results — but that is exactly the scope of this measurement (resource pressure, not lossless-ness). (2) n_regs at the cap reads 255 for both C3 and C4; that is ptxas clamping at the 255-reg/thread architectural cap (real behavior), and the C4 prediction (256) reading near the clamped 255 is coincidental, not an echo — the separate, real n_spills values (636 vs 96) carry the actual signal and differ. (3) Could not independently re-run the GPU harness here (CPU-only adversarial pass, GPU serialized), so verification is by code-path audit + divergence analysis of the recorded artifacts rather than a fresh launch; the divergence-from-prediction evidence is strong enough to rule out echoing.
